newsitem.title: NORWAY: Three shutdowns planned at Saga's Vigdis N.Sea fie.
newsitem.headline: Three shutdowns planned at Saga's Vigdis N.Sea fie.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Wednesday three brief shutdowns at the North Sea Vigdis oilfield were planned for late May and early June because of problems at the nearby Snorre platform.

"The shutdowns will last for up to 24 hours each," Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag told Reuters. "The reason is a change of risers from a subsea system frame to Snorre, to which Vigdis is linked up."

Production at Vigdis resumed last Friday following a month-long unscheduled shutdown caused by problems with the gas compressor. Vigdis output was shut in on April 15 after a vibration was discovered in the compressor unit.
Average output at the field, which came on stream at the end of January five months ahead of schedule, was around 45,000 barrels per day (bpd) on Tuesday, Schiebevaag said.
"The commissioning phase is still going on," he said. "We now plan to increase production at Vigdis to 75,000 bpd at the end of June."
